correctness.rationale: The upper bound is a positive linear combination of the two necessary sample inequalities at j=m and j=m-1. The proposed coefficient attains both contacts. After reindexing j=m-r, every remaining sample is exactly one of two quadratics in y=sin((2r+1)alpha/2); monotonicity handles even r, while the odd quadratic has one negative and one positive root and its positive root is the first odd sample. Symmetry covers the full cycle. Equality in the positive contact combination forces both contacts and hence the unique b. No finite computation is used for the universal quantifier.

originality.rationale: The exact diagonal family N=2m+1, m>=4 was compared against the general continuous/discrete Carathéodory–Fejér framework, a general singleton sampling-rigidity result, and exact fixed-harmonic sampled formulas. The closest results either provide only the framework/qualitative strict-gain criterion or cover the excluded low cases m=2 and m=3. None of the inspected statements implies the displayed closed form or the unique anti-Nyquist extremizer for all m>=4.

value.rationale: The family is structurally natural: m=(N-1)/2 is the highest nonredundant frequency on every odd cyclic group, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem gives the exact sampled constant and unique extremizer for all m>=4, sharpening a prior qualitative sampling-rigidity result to a closed form on an infinite diagonal. The proof exposes a reusable two-contact/two-quadratic mechanism, and the exact asymptotic quantifies the sampling gain.
